name: What happens if my primary bathroom has mold or water damage?

mainEntity.name: How should a remodel handle mold, rot, or water damage found behind the shower or tub walls?
mainEntity.text: How should a remodel handle mold, rot, or water damage found behind the shower or tub walls?

acceptedAnswer.text: If mold, rot, or water damage is found during a primary bathroom remodel, the damage should be fully addressed before the room is rebuilt. That usually means removing affected drywall, insulation, subfloor sections, or framing, then identifying the source of the moisture problem. Fixing the leak or failed waterproofing is essential, or the issue will return after the remodel is finished. This is one reason bathroom projects often uncover added scope. Hidden damage can extend the schedule and budget, but skipping proper repairs risks much bigger costs later. A qualified contractor should document the condition, explain the repair plan, and install new waterproofing correctly before finishes go back on. Homeowners should never accept a cosmetic cover-up over active moisture problems.
acceptedAnswer.description: If mold, rot, or water damage is found, the damaged material should be removed and the cause fixed before new finishes are installed. Simply covering the problem usually leads to future leaks and repairs. The remodel scope may need to expand to include subfloor repair, framing replacement, and improved waterproofing.
